newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shippers press KLM to drop surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shippers press KLM to drop surcharge.

text.p: EVO, the Dutch shippers' organisation, has called on KLM Royal Dutch Airlines to drop its fuel surcharge.
Hans Leijgraaff, EVO spokesman, said the organisation had sent a letter to the Dutch airline last Friday.
"Kerosene prices have dropped tremendously so we have called for an immediate withdrawal of the fuel surcharge," he told Reuters.
He added that the letter was also a consequence of Delta Airline's decision -- announced on March 13 -- to drop the surcharge with immediate effect.

Quoting Shell Aviation's kerosene prices per tonne, Leijgraaff said in January last year prices stood at U.S. $187 per tonne and then this increased to $197 per tonne in July last year, before rising to an October peak of $265 per tonne.
This year, kerosene prices stood at $246 per tonne in January and $205 per tonne in February, he added.

"This year the prices have seen a substantial decrease. Many airlines said they would drop the surcharge once the fuel prices reached last July's levels, but so far there are no signs of them doing this," he said.
